title: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics | Image | Page 15
text:
[IMAGE] This image illustrates a classic mathematical proof by contradiction to show that the square root of 2 (√2) is an irrational number.

The proof starts by assuming that √2 is rational, meaning it can be written as a fraction \( \frac{p}{q} \) where \( p \) and \( q \) are integers with no common factors (lowest terms). It then follows through logical steps: squaring both sides to get \( p^2 = 2q^2 \), and deducing that both \( p \) and \( q \) must be even numbers. This leads to a contradiction because if both \( p \) and \( q \) are even, they share a common factor of 2, contradicting the initial assumption that \( \frac{p}{q} \) is in its lowest terms. Hence, √2 cannot be rational. Source: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics, Page 15

text: [IMAGE] This image illustrates the concept of **similar shapes with varying scales**, often used to explain the idea of **proportional growth** or **scaling factors** in geometry. The series of cauliflower shapes demonstrates how an object can increase in size uniformly while maintaining the same shape, which is a practical example of **three-dimensional scaling**. This visual can help students understand how linear dimensions, surface area, and volume change when objects are scaled up or down proportionally. Source: NCERT Grade 9 Mathematics, Page 17
